title: Count only subscription-backed sessions as Codex usage
head: dab5dadb746a
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: fix verified for reported case; one narrow finding (copied-fork inherited session_meta drops child usage), README/comment accuracy, optional legacy-fixture test note, interactions with open PRs #12803 and #12595

leads.summary: Combining open PR #12803's prefilter with this provider check silently restores foreign-provider usage
leads.consequence: #12803's added substring gate discards every normal session_meta line before the new guard sees it. Both non-OpenAI rollouts and their model totals are counted again; the normal cache and usage record then publish the inflated totals. An exact three-way merge produced no conflict markers, so this is easy to miss. Include session_meta in the prefilter and exercise both tests together.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus (#12803 pre-filter defeats check; combo run 15550)

leads.summary: #12595's incremental file cache needs a provider-filter port and invalidation, not just a merge resolution
leads.consequence: The other PR moves native parsing into read_native_codex_session, so git merge-file conflicts around the whole function. Picking its scanner without moving this PR's guard loses the fix. Even when the guard is ported, a machine that ran #12595 first retains schema-1 per-file totals for unchanged foreign rollouts indefinitely, because reusable_record checks only mtime and size, not scanner logic, and that cache has no age limit. Normal refresh keeps the wrong totals, while --force corrects them. Move the guard into the new parser and bump FILE_CACHE_SCHEMA or otherwise invalidate that file cache on deployment.
leads.triage: new; verified by coordinator (coord/merged.12595 one conflict region, coord/pr-12595.diff reusable_record mtime+size, FILE_CACHE_SCHEMA) and Opus check2 port run (10010 without bump, 110 with bump or --force); 'indefinitely' narrowed to the 30-day window

leads.summary: Copied-fork rollouts can contain inherited foreign session_meta, hiding the fork's subscription usage
leads.consequence: At Codex CLI 0.154.0 a copied fork can have its own openai session_meta first, then a parent ollama session_meta copied into its initial history before the new turns. The scanner breaks at the parent metadata and counts none of the child's subsequent paid tokens or sessions. Only the rollout's own first metadata should determine a whole-file exclusion, or inherited records should be distinguished before counting.

leads.summary: The `openai` provider id is not evidence that Codex tokens were paid by a subscription
leads.consequence: Codex CLI can write model_provider=openai for an API-key session billed to OpenAI's API, or for a config with openai_base_url aimed at localhost or another gateway. The new code includes those files and describes their tokens as subscription-backed, and the panel can label a missing plan as Subscription. The new README's absolute 'Every collector counts only the turns its own subscription paid for' and 'a local model never shows up' are therefore not assured; the comment that every non-openai id must be custom is also false because Ollama, LM Studio, and both Bedrock IDs are built in. Either narrow the guarantee to a provider-ID filter, or determine actual auth/endpoint before claiming subscription-only accounting.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus README/openai-id findings; panel 'Subscription' label is the plan-tier label, not published

leads.summary: Legacy fixture omits session_meta, so the new test cannot catch rejecting real old metadata without a provider
leads.consequence: The promised legacy behavior is conditional on a session_meta object with no model_provider. The test instead writes no session_meta at all. A plausible refactor from `if provider and provider != NATIVE_PROVIDER` to `if provider != NATIVE_PROVIDER` still passes all 22 assertions, yet excludes actual old files. Add a fixture with `session_meta.payload` present but without model_provider and assert that its tokens/session/model remain.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus legacy-fixture gap; mutant claim confirmed by coordinator reading of fixture and by Opus check2 run

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the provider check fixes the reported case. Rollouts whose `session_meta.payload.model_provider` is `ollama`, `lmstudio`, `amazon-bedrock` or a custom id are dropped. `openai` rollouts, and rollouts with no or a null provider, still count. Limits (app-server RPC) are untouched. Against Codex CLI source at `rust-v0.154.0`:

- Codex writes the provider on `session_meta` and not on `turn_context`.
- `--oss` records `ollama` or `lmstudio`.
- A user `model_providers` entry cannot redefine the built-in `openai` id.

In an isolated run, `test/shell.d/agent-usage-codex-scanner-test.sh` passes 22/22 on the head and on the PR applied to the current `quattro` tip. The new case fails against the base collector with the message quoted in the description (15550 tokens instead of 150).

One narrow correctness gap and a few accuracy notes follow.

### A forked rollout can carry a second, inherited `session_meta`

The new comment says the field "is written once, on the first record", but upstream Codex says otherwise: "Later SessionMeta lines can be copied from fork history" (`codex-rs/rollout/src/recorder.rs:1053-1055`). A copied fork writes the child's own `session_meta` first (`codex-rs/rollout/src/recorder.rs:1803-1806`), then the parent's items, including the parent's `session_meta` (`codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs:1480-1518`). The loop `break`s on any foreign `session_meta`, so a copied fork whose child runs on `openai` and whose parent ran on another provider is dropped completely, including the child's own turns.

Synthetic rollout, today's tokens:

```text
line 1  session_meta  model_provider=openai   (child's own)
line 2  session_meta  model_provider=ollama   (copied from parent)
        parent turns  9900 tokens
        child turns    110 tokens

base collector: 10010   head: 0   subscription usage: 110
```

**Impact:** in 0.154.0 this mainly affects forked subagents and forks of older-format threads, and only when parent and child providers differ.

**Suggested change:** track the provider per segment instead of stopping at the first foreign record: each `session_meta` sets it, and the `thread_settings_applied` event's `model_provider_id`, which Codex writes after the copied prefix, updates it (`codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs:2184-2213`). In the example above this gives 110 and the scanner test still passes 22/22. Letting only the first `session_meta` decide is simpler but reports 10010 here, because it also counts the copied parent turns. Either way, the "written once" comment needs correcting. A copied fork also repeats the parent's `token_count` lines, which the collector already counted twice before this PR, so no simple rule is exact for these files.

### README and code comments state a stronger guarantee than the check provides

- "Every collector counts only the turns its own subscription paid for" does not hold for the Claude collector: `scan_projects()` in `bin/omarchy-agent-usage-claude` has no provider filter, as the PR description itself notes.
- The built-in `openai` id also covers API-key auth, and the `openai_base_url` setting points that same id at any endpoint (`codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/lib.rs:293-311`, `codex-rs/config/src/config_toml.rs:400-401`). So "limited to turns the subscription actually served" and "a local model never shows up as subscription usage" are stronger than the check. "Limited to sessions on Codex's built-in `openai` provider (or with no provider recorded)" would be accurate.
- The `NATIVE_PROVIDER` comment "Any other id is a custom provider in config.toml" misses the built-in `ollama`, `lmstudio`, `amazon-bedrock` and `amazon-bedrock-runtime` ids. Dropping them is still correct.

**Suggested change:** scope the "Every collector" sentence to Codex and describe the filter by provider id.

**Optional test improvement:** the legacy fixture writes no `session_meta` line at all. Older Codex releases wrote a `session_meta` without `model_provider` (checked at 0.40.0 and 0.50.0; the field is present from 0.51.0). A variant that also drops rollouts whose `session_meta` lacks a provider would therefore still pass all 22 assertions. Giving the legacy fixture a `session_meta` line with no `model_provider` pins the real older shape, which the current code already handles.

### Interaction with open PRs touching the same loop

- **#12803** ("Pre-filter Codex session lines before JSON parsing") skips every line without `"token_count"` or `"turn_context"` before parsing. Its collector hunk applies without a text conflict, but the combination never sees `session_meta`: with both collector changes, this PR's test reports 15550 tokens instead of 150.
- **#12595** ("Read only the session files that changed since the last scan") moves this loop into `read_native_codex_session()` and conflicts textually with this change. It also adds a per-file cache that replays a file's totals while its mtime and size are unchanged. If #12595 lands first and this guard is ported without bumping `FILE_CACHE_SCHEMA`, cached totals for unchanged files keep their foreign-provider tokens until the files leave the 30-day window or a `--force` scan runs.

**Impact:** combined with #12803 as it stands, foreign-provider tokens are counted again with no error; only this PR's scanner test catches it. A #12595 port without a schema bump does the same for cached files.

**Suggested change:** whichever of these lands second adds `"session_meta"` to the #12803 pre-filter, and a port onto #12595 bumps `FILE_CACHE_SCHEMA`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Collector source reviewed against Codex CLI source at tag `rust-v0.154.0` (older tags for the legacy format). Scanner test and synthetic rollout scenarios (forks, `--oss` providers, legacy and null providers, combinations with #12803 and a port onto #12595) run in an isolated sandbox. No real Codex binary or real session history was used. The full `test/shell` suite was not rerun; no other test references the changed files. How often forked or provider-switching sessions occur in practice was not measured.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
